title: Lever Sign Test

positions.as_written: With the patient supine and the leg extended, place a closed fist under the proximal third of the calf.
Compare with the other side, which matters here as much as in every other test in this chapter.
Record what happened to the heel, which is the observation the test rests on.
A partial lift is difficult to interpret and should be recorded as such rather than forced into a binary result.
It follows that the test should not add information about structures other than the anterior cruciate, and claims that it does should be treated sceptically.
